$comment: Availability, notice period and relocation willingness — lifted verbatim from
apps/ai-service/app/profiling/signals.py.
BOTH FAMILIES EXIST BECAUSE THEY WERE FABRICATING. Issue #424 follow-up and issue #437,
each a measured post-merge finding, not a hypothesis:
availability — the cues were BARE SUBSTRINGS, and 'abhi' merely means 'right now'. The
question bank's OWN questions open with it ('Abhi kis sheher mein hain?'), so the natural
answer to our own question invented an availability the worker never stated:
'abhi pune me hu'        -> {current_location: Pune, availability: immediate}
'6 month ka experience'  -> availability: notice_period
'freelance kaam karta hu'-> availability: immediate
relocation — same shape, 16/16 shop-floor phrases: 'bahar' matched 'bahar ka diameter',
'shift' matched 'night shift', 'ready' matched 'job ready hai'.
Both are LIVE fields: availability is a reach scoring signal (reach.job-source.ts) and both
render on the worker's resume. We were telling payers a worker could start immediately on
the strength of an adverb in our own question.
THE RULE: a cue must be a GENUINE statement, matched with boundaries and with adjacency —
a place next to a going verb, a time adverb next to a join intent. The decision is made in
ONE place with adjacency, never by hoping a keyword list is unambiguous.
FAIL DIRECTION IS TOWARD 'unknown'. availability is a MUST_ASK topic, so an undetected one
is simply asked. A FABRICATED one is never corrected.
$comment_fragments: The cue lists are BUILT from these pieces, recombined ten different ways. Inlining them
would put ten copies of each alternation in this file, which is exactly the drift this
package exists to prevent. `{PLACE}` nests `{ANYWHERE}`, so expansion is a fixed point.
ANYWHERE_DEV is a SEPARATE fragment from ANYWHERE and uses {DB}/{DE}, not {WB}/{WE}. A word
boundary does not work after a Devanagari matra, so wrapping these tokens in {WB}...{WE}
would make them silently dead — the exact failure mode that costs a detector with no error.
NUM carries [0-9०-९] rather than \d for the same reason salary.json does: Python's \d
already matched Devanagari digits, and only the enumeration preserves that in both engines.
$comment_anywhereCues: A generality-of-place idiom gives 'anywhere' PRECEDENCE over any state named in the same
message: the worker said anywhere, so a state beside it is context, not the preference.
'kahin bhi ja sakta hu, abhi Gujarat me kaam kar raha hu' -> ['Gujarat'] without this
$comment_relocateCues: ADJACENCY IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. 'bahar'/'outside' are a PLACE and never a cue alone, because
'bahar JAANA' is leaving town while 'bahar KA diameter' is the outer diameter — only the verb
beside it decides. 'dusre sheher' likewise: on its own it is as often work history as an
intention. 'chalega' alone is the machine verb ('vmc chalega mujhe'). 'ready' must attach to
a MOVE, so 'ready hu machine ke liye' has nothing to attach to and stays unset. 'shift' must
take a becoming-form, so 'night shift karta hu' and 'general shift' never fire.
$comment_immediateStrong: The word itself is the answer, whoever is speaking — no blocker needed. A time adverb next
to a join/start intent is the ONLY way 'abhi'/'aaj'/'kal' can contribute, and that is the
BARE `ready` IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT (adversarial review of #436, HIGH-1). An earlier cut
ended this alternation with `|ready)`, which combined with adverb-adjacency to re-create the
exact bug class in the register it most needed to protect: on a shop floor 'job' means the
WORKPIECE, and 'ready' is what you say about a part, a tool, a fixture or a drawing.
'job abhi ready hai' / 'tool aaj ready ho jayega' -> immediate
$comment_immediateSelfState: 'I am, right now, not working / free / ready.' Real answers, but every one is SUBJECT- and
TENSE-sensitive, so each is additionally gated on the selfState blockers below.
FIRST PERSON IS REQUIRED (review of #436, HIGH-2). An earlier cut accepted `hai`/`hain` and
justified it with 'the copula makes this safe'. That was wrong: they are THIRD person, so
objects became available workers — 'machine free hai', 'wo free hai'.
'available' carries a trailing negative lookahead so 'koi job available hai kya?' — a
question about vacancies — is not read as a start date.
$comment_immediateNegationBearing: These carry a negator INSIDE the phrase, and that negator is what makes them mean available
('kaam nahi kar raha' = 'I am not working' = free). They are therefore EXEMPT from the
negation veto — vetoing them would delete the very positives the veto exists to protect.
Held as their own list so the exemption is a property of the CUE, declared once, rather than
a special case buried in the matching loop.
`hai`, `mil raha` and `milta` were DROPPED (review of #436, MEDIUM-3): 'yahan acha kaam nahi
milta' is a complaint about the current job, and 'kaam nahi hai' is as often the shop's

WINDOWED, not whole-message, so a later unrelated clause cannot suppress a real answer.
$comment_preNegatorLookback: How many word-tokens before a cue are scanned for a PRE-POSED negator. Two: enough for
'turant nahi aa sakta' and 'abhi nahi join kar sakta', tight enough that a negator elsewhere
in the clause cannot reach the cue ('kaam nahi milta isliye turant join kar sakta hu' — the
WHY THIS EXISTS AT ALL: the negation engine masks BACKWARD, because Hindi normally negates
after what it negates ('ITI nahi kiya'). Negated ABILITY inverts that word order — the
negator comes FIRST — so the backward mask covers 'turant'/'abhi' and leaves the ability verb,
which is the cue we match on, untouched. For most families missing that is the safe
direction. For availability it is NOT: the cue still fires and records the OPPOSITE of what
$comment_noticeCues: Durations deliberately EXCLUDE 'saal'/'year': years are experience, never a notice period —
and the experience clause is precisely what the old bare 'month'/'mahina'/'days' cues were
A duration only means NOTICE when it is the time something TAKES ('15 din lagenge', '30 din
baad'). A duration on its own ('6 month ka experience hai') says nothing about availability.
$comment_askedNotice: Read ONLY when the availability question is the one that was just asked. These phrasings are
real answers to 'join karne mein kitne din lagenge?' but say nothing on their own in the
middle of a transcript — running them context-free is how '6 month' became a notice period.
The span variant is a SEPARATE pattern rather than groups added to the one above, because
that one is used in boolean contexts where a group change would be an invisible behaviour
$comment_askedNoticeBlockers: Even in availability context a duration is only a NOTICE if it is time-UNTIL, not time-since
or a work pattern (review of #436, MEDIUM-5). `last_asked` means 'the last question we
asked', NOT 'the question this message answers', so while availability is pending the worker
may still be talking about something else:
'10 din pehle join kiya tha'   -> was notice_period (time AGO)
'hafte me 6 din kaam karta hu' -> was notice_period (a work WEEK)
'do mahine se salary nahi mili'-> was notice_period (time SINCE)
'X se' is 'for the last X' while 'X baad'/'X mein' is 'in X' — the distinction that separates
all three from a real notice period.

'whenever you say' — genuinely immediate. Matched EXPLICITLY so it stops being read as

The bare time adverb IS the answer to 'how many days to join?', but only when it is the WHOLE
answer. ANCHORED AT BOTH ENDS (review of #436, HIGH-1): an earlier cut anchored only the
start, so any long sentence opening with a time word was read as a start date —
'kal meri shaadi hai to ready rahunga' -> immediate.
{JOIN} alone is the ability to join with no immediacy adverb attached. The last entry is a
time adverb next to a bare CAN-DO verb: 'abhi kar sakta hun' answering 'join karne mein
kitne din lagenge?' means 'I can start now', while the same words answering anything else
could be about the WORK. Measured on an owner session — 'abhi kar sakta hun package de doge
toh' stays unknown, because {JOIN} requires an explicit join/start verb and this has none.
Bare 'abhi' remains barred from the CONTEXT-FREE table for the documented reason: our own
{NWC} not \W: the anchors must bracket the same character set in both engines.
